newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $0.50-trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by hefty hog marketings on Wednesday and outlooks for active runs Thursday, dealers and packer buyers said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog marketings Tuesday were 116,000 head, above the estimate of 110,000, USDA said. The Wednesday estimate was 110,000 head, which several dealers said was likely filled.
Hog runs swelled as some producers shipped animals they had been holding back since late last week when prices rallied, in hopes of capitalizing on possible further gains.
The gains were posted on news Taiwan suspended pork exports.
Producers started working on becoming current in their marketings again, once cash prices rose above $50.00-$51.00 early Tuesday, especially with hog weights increasing.

Iowa/southern Minnesota direct hogs weekly average weight of barrows and gilts for the week ended Saturday last week was 254.1 lbs, up from 253.6 lbs the previous week and well above 246.9 lbs a year ago, USDA reported on Wednesday.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices Thursday at plants could range $50.00-$50.50, sources there said.
Indiana and Ohio top values could span $49.50-$50.00, sources said.

Illinois top prices at plants were seen at $51.00-$52.00, reflecting a $1.00 premium over USDA's top quote that at least one major packer was willing to pay to ensure it had enough hogs to meet scheduled slaughter needs, private sources said.
